x: Below: Heptathlete Julie Hollman set a tremendous score of over 6000 points in the Multistars Meet at Desenzano del Garda, Italy, in May but was beset by problems when the major Games came around later in the year and unable to reproduce her best form.

Now turning to individual performances, in the major worldwide championships, seven Belgravians qualified for the World Athletic Championships; Sean Baldock, Tim Benjamin, Dwain Chambers, (who achieved a silver medal in the 4 x 100 m), Julie Hollman, Rachel King, Shelley Newman and Amy Spencer.

Julie Hollman was not best pleased with her long jump but delighted with her 1.81m high jump - a season's best. Our triple jumpers excelled with a longest ever leap from David Wellstead and a best since '96 from Caroline Stead - both aided by the stiff breeze.
Despite the conditions there were some positive results from our intrepid heptathletes, Julie Hollman and Maureen Knight, doubling up to win both 100m hurdles and shot putts.

Women. 100m: 1r1 S.Claxton 12.03/0.8; 4r2 A.Onuora U20 12.09/-0.6; 4r3 A.Spencer U20 11.97/-1.8. 100mH: 1r2 R.King 13.38/-0.6. 400mH: 1r1 J.Culley 60.34; 2r2 M.Carey 60.75; 3r2 H.Stares 61.19. LJ: 2 J.Hollman 6.11/0.5. TJ: 4 C.Stead 12.16/2.4; DT: 2 S.Newman 56.90.
Then, teaming up with fellow multi-eventer Julie Hollman, these two covered the sprint hurdles and high jump to pull in more maximum points.

Women. 800m: a 4h3 C Robinson 2:07.73. 5000m: 3 C Berry 16:01.38; dnf B Dagne. 100mH: a 5h2 J Hollman 14.12/-0.3. 400mH: b 4 M Carey 57.77 (a 2h2 M Carey 57.63); 4h1 J Culley 1:00.41; dq h2 M Marks; 5h4 H Stares 1:03.77.
With Julie Hollman in the line-up, no-one was going to get near our sprint hurdle duo, and as Julie then turned her attention to the shot where she partnered Eva Massey, it was top points again.
